pages.text: "I'm hungry! Bread first!" Mina grabbed flatbread with muddy hands. A muddy print pressed into its white surface. The fallen river had left wide mud in front of the yard.
Mina brought it toward their mouth. "Oh, there's dirt on it." Beside Mina, youngest child Sonu dipped hands into the water tub.
Sitting on the platform, Mina looked at the bread. Every touch added dirt. "I'm trying to wipe it off, but it gets dirtier."
Mom opened Mina's palm. Mud filled every crease. "Dirt moved from your hands to the bread. Let's wash first."
Mom took Mina to the tub. One dipperful loosened the mud. "Even water does this?" Mina turned their hands over.
Mom offered soap. Mina made bubbles, rubbing palms, backs, and between fingers. Sonu rubbed little hands beside them.
Mina rinsed off the bubbles with clean water. Muddy water ran away. "I can see my palm lines again!"
Mom dried both children's hands with a towel. Mina picked up fresh bread. This time, no dirt marked the white surface.
The next day, Mina washed after playing again. Waving clean hands, Mina called, "Sonu, wash yours, too!"
Sonu hugged Mina tightly. Fresh bread was in Mina's hand. "Clean Hands—Yum! Let's eat together."
